record.original_question: Let T113(a,b;3) denote the weighted sum of all tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations and all three bone orientations are allowed, where a tiling with m stones has weight 3^m. Is the sequence T113(n, 2n-4; 3), defined for n >= 5, 2-adically continuous as a function of n?

evidence.quote: Let Tijk (a, b; 3) denote the weighted sum of the i, j, k tilings of the (a, b)-benzel as defined near the end of section 1, where a tiling with m stones has weight 3^m.
Problem 17: Is T113 (n, 2n - 4; 3) 2-adically continuous as a function of n >= 5?
The sequence appears to be constant mod 2, constant mod 4, constant mod 8, and 8-periodic mod 16.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the triangular grid in the plane, and for positive integers $a,b$ define the $(a,b)$-benzel as the hexagonal region introduced as follows: take the set of unit triangles whose centroids $(x,y)$ in suitable coordinates satisfy a fixed system of six linear inequalities depending on $a$ and $b$ that cut out a centrally symmetric hexagonal subregion of the triangular grid (the "benzel"). The prototiles used to tile the benzel are:
- "stones": trihexes consisting of three pairwise adjacent unit triangles meeting at a vertex (two possible orientations, "up" and "down");
- "bones": trihexes consisting of three unit triangles whose centroids are collinear (three possible orientations, corresponding to the three directions in the triangular grid).

For a subset $S \subseteq \{1,2\}$ of allowed stone orientations and $T \subseteq \{1,2,3\}$ of allowed bone orientations, let the "$ijk$-tilings" of the $(a,b)$-benzel be the tilings using only the selected stone and bone orientations, where $i=|S|$, $j=|T|$. Define
$$T_{113}(a,b;3) \;=\; \sum_{\tau} 3^{m(\tau)},$$
where the sum is over all tilings $\tau$ of the $(a,b)$-benzel that use $1$ stone orientation, and all $3$ bone orientations, and $m(\tau)$ denotes the number of stones in the tiling $\tau$.

A sequence $(a_n)_{n\ge n_0}$ of integers is called $2$-adically continuous in $n$ if the map $n \mapsto a_n$ extends to a continuous function $\mathbb{Z}_2 \to \mathbb{Z}_2$ from the $2$-adic integers to themselves; equivalently, for every $k\ge 1$ there exists $N_k$ such that whenever $n\equiv n'\pmod{2^{N_k}}$ one has $a_n \equiv a_{n'}\pmod{2^k}$.

Question: Is the sequence $\bigl(T_{113}(n,\,2n-4;\,3)\bigr)_{n\ge 5}$ $2$-adically continuous as a function of $n$?
artifact.status_search_result: A follow-up work on benzel tilings via generalized compression (arXiv:2403.07663) revisits problems posed about weighted benzel tilings, but no explicit resolution of 2-adic continuity for the weighted sequence T_{113}(n, 2n-4; 3) appears in the literature found. The problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Tilings of benzels via generalized compression
status_evidence.snippet: Follow-up paper on benzel tilings extending compression methods; does not appear to resolve the 2-adic continuity question for T_{113}(n,2n-4;3).
status_evidence.claim: No explicit resolution found in this follow-up work.

status_evidence.snippet: Hub page tracking benzel tiling problems and updates.
status_evidence.claim: No update indicating this 2-adic continuity problem has been resolved.
